question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $12,$ the additive inverse of $-18$ modulo $12$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-18$ modulo $12$ is the integer $0\le x<12$ such that

$$
x+(-18)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,12).
$$

First, we note that $-18≡6\,(\text{mod}\,12):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-18 & ≡(-2)\cdot 12+6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡(-2)\cdot 0+6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-6+6≡0,$ so $x≡-6\,(\text{mod}\,12).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡0-6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡12-6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\  & ≡6 & \,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-18$ modulo $12$ is $6.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-18+6≡-12≡(-1)\cdot 12≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
